primitives.note: Void Shift's crowd control immunity and 90% damage reduction only reduce damage Malzahar takes; irrelevant to the damage-dealing fight but relevant to a survival fight if Malzahar is the tank.
Call of the Void deals its AoE magic damage 0.4s after cast, on a 6s cooldown.
Mana costs (60-80 Q, 40-60 W, 60-100 E, 100 R) can meaningfully gate cast frequency over a 15s fight depending on mana pool/regen.
Void Swarm summons one or more Voidlings that independently deal on-hit magic damage (base + level scaling + AD/AP ratios) for their duration.
Malzahar gains a Zz'Rot Swarm stack (cap 2) per ability cast; W consumes all stacks to summon extra Voidlings, so more Q/E casts before a W cast means more summoned pets.
Malefic Visions ticks every 0.25s over 4s; Nether Grasp's tether beam ticks every 0.25s over 2.5s and its Null Zone ticks every 0.5s over 5s.
Nether Grasp channels for up to 2.5s dealing beam damage, during which Malzahar's other actions are constrained (channel interrupts on movement/most actions after a short grace period).

needsBespoke.why: All damage-fight-relevant mechanics (delayed-cast AoE, a self-stacking resource that determines summon count, a summoned pet with on-hit damage, and a channel that produces both a beam DoT and a separate zone DoT) map onto existing primitives (plain-cast, ramping-per-cast, pet-or-summon, dot, charge-or-channel, resource-budget).

unsettled.question: Does re-casting Malefic Visions (E) on a target that is already infected refresh/extend the 4s DoT window (allowing more total ticks over the fight), or does it just re-apply from the current tick count with no net gain, effectively wasting the recast for damage purposes?
options: Recast fully refreshes the DoT to a new 4s/16-tick window, adding to total damage over the fight
Recast has no additional effect if the debuff is already active (only Q/R hits refresh it), so an E recast on an already-infected target is a wasted cast for damage
quotes: which refreshes upon damaging them with ''{{ai|Call of the Void|Malzahar}}'' or ''{{ai|Nether Grasp|Malzahar}}''

unsettled.question: The tether beam's 0.25s tick interval (10 ticks over 2.5s) and the Null Zone's 0.5s tick interval (10 ticks over 5s) are not stated directly by any single bin field, only implied by dividing BeamDamage/BeamAPRatio by BeamDamageTicks=10 and by the tooltip's *0.05 factor for the zone. Is the actual per-tick cadence exactly as inferred, and do both dots really run the full stated duration against a stationary target in the damage-fight sim?
options: Tick cadence and durations are exactly as inferred (0.25s beam ticks, 0.5s zone ticks) with no extra hidden ticks or truncation
The true tick cadence differs (e.g. zone applies fewer/more discrete hits or has an initial/final tick offset), changing how many times on-hit/on-tick item effects trigger

unsettled.question: Void Swarm's level-scaling flat damage term is given by the wiki as a non-linear pp formula but by the bin as an exactly linear byLevel row (+3.5/level); which is the true live value used to compute Voidling attack damage?
options: Use the bin's exact linear byLevel values (source of truth for game data)
Use the wiki's displayed pp formula, which may reflect a more current/tested in-game curve despite disagreeing with the bin row

unsettled.question: A Zz'Rot Swarm stack is granted 'per cast, not per activation.' For Call of the Void, whose damage/silence lands 0.4s after cast, does the stack for W's bonus Voidling get granted at the moment of the Q cast (immediately) or only once Q's effect resolves — which matters for tight rotation sequencing inside a 15s window?
options: Stack is granted immediately on cast input, before the 0.4s delayed effect resolves
Stack is only granted once the ability's effect actually completes/resolves
quotes: ''Zz'Rot Swarm'' stacks are gained per cast and not per ability activation.

proposal: If Nether Grasp (R) is available at fight start, cast it first on the dummy to lock in its long beam DoT and Null Zone as early as possible, since its 80-140s cooldown means it can likely only be cast once (or not at all, depending on assumed level) within the 15s window.
Immediately follow with (or open with, if R is unavailable or on cooldown) Malefic Visions (E) on the dummy to start its damage-over-time ticking as early as possible.
Cast Call of the Void (Q) on the dummy; its delayed AoE damage both deals direct damage and refreshes Malefic Visions' DoT.
Cast Void Swarm (W) to consume the Zz'Rot Swarm stacks accumulated from the R/E/Q casts, summoning one or more Voidlings to add ongoing on-hit magic damage.

For the remainder of the 15s window, recast Q and E on cooldown, using each Q (and R, if it comes off cooldown) hit to keep Malefic Visions' DoT continuously refreshed on the dummy, and recast W whenever it is off cooldown and stacks are available.
questions: At what champion level/rank is Nether Grasp assumed available, and given its 80-140s cooldown, should the simulated fight assume it is cast once, cast at all, or excluded entirely from a 15s window?
Is opening with R (to start its long cooldown early) or opening with E (to start the long DoT early, potentially losing R's Q-refresh interaction) the higher-damage choice for a 15s fight?
Should recasting Malefic Visions on an already-infected target be included in the optimal rotation at all, given the unresolved question of whether it actually refreshes/extends the DoT window?

Does the simulator model Voidling pet uptime, movement to the target, and their individual attack cadence, or does it need a simplified assumption (e.g. instant engage, fixed attack speed) for how many attacks each summoned Voidling lands within its duration?
